A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same StageRoute research despite the changed title and organization. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original StageRoute simulation results and RouterBench evaluations in Sections 6.1–6.2, including reward, regret, and model-selection outcomes.

after.justification: V2 reports original RouterBench experiments in Section 5 and synthetic evaluations in Appendix E, including regret, deployment decisions, and performance-cost trajectories.

M1.justification: StageRoute retains the same deployment optimization, reward UCBs, cost LCBs, per-query routing LP, sampling, and feedback updates. V2 expands the deployment MIP formulation and discusses contextual compatibility without specifying an implemented procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight RouterBench tasks, 36,497 queries, and 11 candidate LLMs, plus the same 15-model synthetic suite. V2's discussion of newer models refers to coverage already present in v1; moving that suite to Appendix E does not add coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds the uniform-sampling baseline, labeled Random in plots, to both experimental suites. It also directly compares RouterBench deployment decisions and performance-cost outcomes against the Oracle; v1's RouterBench Figure 6 shows only StageRoute and Greedy. The related-work comparison table is not an empirical baseline evaluation.

E3.justification: RouterBench's confidence parameter changes from 0.2 to 0.1 and its budget from 0.0002 to a default 0.001, with additional 0.002-budget evaluation. V2 introduces capacity and update-interval sweeps and reports regret and cost/deployment diagnostics beyond v1's cumulative-reward plot. Synthetic initialization changes from six available models to five, and its tested middle concurrency cap changes from six to five.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands RouterBench analysis through Oracle-versus-StageRoute heatmaps, performance-cost trajectories, and sensitivity to concurrency, update interval, and budget. Synthetic sweeps are revised, while v1's individual model-selection trace disappears. Appendix Figure 6(b) and 6(f) repeat the same plot, leaving the independence of that synthetic budget comparison unclear.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results are averaged over 10 independent runs. Neither reports seed identities, confidence intervals, significance tests, or defined uncertainty bands. Changes to the algorithm's confidence parameter concern experimental settings, not statistical reporting.

E6.justification: V2 replaces or adds substantial experimental results, including RouterBench regret curves, Oracle-tracking heatmaps, cost trajectories, and revised synthetic curves. New findings include lowest RouterBench regret at 1000-round updates and higher regret under the larger tested budget. These are results under revised settings, not established same-setting improvements over v1. The two model-statistics tables retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 changes the stated stage-count condition from K=Omega(T^(1/3)) to K=Theta(T^(1/3)). Theorem 2 explicitly specifies piecewise-stationary instances and arbitrary update frequency and concurrency cap. V2 adds a budget-violation-order assertion and removes v1's contextual Omega(T) regret statement. The detailed upper- and lower-bound proofs otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The central StageRoute, near-optimal-regret, and Oracle-tracking contributions remain. V2 adds an explicit first-joint-formulation claim and presents compatibility with contextual estimators as an algorithmic contribution, whereas v1 discusses contextual extensions as future work.

C2.justification: V2 removes v1's substantive warning that context-dependent rewards or costs can defeat the noncontextual estimates, including the stated linear-regret failure condition. It adds interpretations of average-budget feasibility, Uniform's apparent advantage through overspending, and increased regret under larger budgets through a stronger Oracle and fixed confidence parameter. These materially change the discussion of applicability and experimental findings.

D1.justification: V2 documents binary activation variables for the deployment MIP, reward clipping in the Gaussian simulations, runtime estimates, alternative solvers, and possible warm starts. Gurobi version and hardware remain unchanged. Conversely, Appendix E no longer explicitly states v1's synthetic default budget of 2, leaving some settings less reproducible. The clipping description does not establish that preprocessing changed.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning through a new routing-framework comparison table and discussion of combinatorial bandits alongside BwK and streaming bandits. It adds relevant citations, including UniRoute, CSCR, RouterDC, and multiple CMAB works, and more explicitly argues that existing frameworks do not address its combined constraints.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, algorithm exposition, and theoretical discussion are extensively rewritten. Related work moves to Appendix A, synthetic experiments move to Appendix E, and RouterBench becomes the main empirical narrative. The title changes, and a conclusion and ethics statement replace the previous closing limitations discussion.

P2.justification: V2 adds a framework-comparison table, paired deployment heatmaps, a performance-cost plot, and reorganized sensitivity panels. The original empirical figures are replaced rather than merely renumbered, while both model-statistics tables move to the appendix. The workflow illustration is retained. Conference formatting also changes typography, headers, and figure arrangements throughout.

improvement.justification: V2's RouterBench deployment and cost diagnostics make the operational claims easier to assess than v1's single reward comparison, while the MIP and runtime explanations improve transparency. These provide a limited net gain. The contextual-failure warning is lost, and unclear synthetic defaults and repeated Figure 6 panels weaken parts of the expanded evaluation. The revision does not establish a same-setting performance improvement or substantially repair the retained proofs.
